prompt:
Repaint the attached grey block-out as ONE finished building sprite for a pastoral isometric railway game.

Style: that of the attached style board. Crisp pixel-art-inspired clustered shading, broad readable masses, three or four shades per material, restrained detail, a strong silhouette. The palette family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B, slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest, lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest.

Camera: keep the block-out's camera exactly. Orthographic 2:1 isometric, ground edges two pixels across for each pixel down, vertical edges vertical, no perspective. Do not rotate or tilt the view. The foot of the lower-left wall runs parallel to the plinth's lower-left edge and the foot of the lower-right wall parallel to its lower-right edge: both walls equally steep, neither flatter than the block-out's. Do not turn the building towards the viewer: the lower-right wall is seen as much from the side as the lower-left wall. Show the whole building with a clear margin all round: nothing touches the edge of the picture.

Footprint: the grey plinth is the building's footprint. The building stands on it and fills it: its outer walls rise from the plinth's edges, and at ground level nothing reaches outside the plinth. Keep the foot of the two visible walls plain and straight from corner to corner, so that it shows where the building stands: no bushes, crates, steps or loose objects in front of it. Above the ground the shape is free: roofs, towers, chimneys and machinery may differ from the block and may overhang a little. The dark openings in the block-out show where the front door, or a depot's train portals, are; keep them in those walls.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building surfaces.

Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow, or loose objects standing apart from the building.

The building is turned half round. The front faces the upper right, away from the camera, and nothing of it is in this picture: no entrance door and none of the front's windows or other features on either visible wall. The lower-left wall is the BACK, plainer than the front; the lower-right wall is the left-hand side.

Diesel age: larger and more industrial, still of the same countryside. Warm brick walls on cream stone bases, riveted iron and steel trusses, slate or corrugated roofs with roof lights, big sliding doors, iron cranes and tanks, forest-green paint.

Fuel Pump. A railway refuelling point for diesel engines

A LONG, NARROW red-brick pump house on cream limestone quoins and base; its
long side is about 2.4 times its short side; walls tall, about 0.45 of the house's width. The long
side has two bays: the door bay (forest-green plank door, lamp over it, a small slate-roofed porch
gable a little forward of the wall), a downpipe, a plain bay, and a big quoined pier at the end.
The short side and the back are plain brick between quoins: no door, no window, no porch, no lamp.
On the house a dark steel frame with X bracing, and on it a riveted forest-green steel tank with
two oat-cream bands, a railing, a manhole and a vent, as long as the long side and as deep as the
house, covering the whole roof. At one end of the long side a tall forest-green hose crane: ONE
post with one diagonal brace and ONE jib, about 0.43 tile long (the width of the short side), the
hose hanging from the jib's end. Pipes with copper bands run from the tank to the crane.
THE LIGHT never turns with the building. It comes from the upper left: tops lightest, the
lower-left wall mid (r0's front, luma 112), the lower-right wall darkest (r0's short side, 67).
Camera: orthographic 2:1 isometric, 30 degrees down, no perspective; both wall feet fall one pixel
for every two across.

View r2. The front faces the upper right, hidden: nothing of the front shows on either visible
wall. The lower-left wall is the BACK: LONG, plain brick between quoins, no door, no porch, two
bays wide, as the lower-right wall of the fourth picture. The lower-right wall is the left-hand
side: SHORT and plain, one bay wide, brick between limestone quoins with a quoined pier at each
end, no door, no window, no porch, no lamp. The tank lies along the lower-left wall and is as long
as it. The crane's post stands at the right corner, where the guide's thin post is, with one
diagonal brace and one jib that rises to the upper right, parallel to the lower-right wall's foot;
the jib is about as long as the short side is wide (about 92 px on the guide), not longer, and the
hose hangs from its end. The post's top stands above the tank's top.

References: the first is the guide, the second the style board. The third is this same building
in view r0, seen from the front, laid onto its footprint at the guide's camera and scale. The
fourth is this building in view r1: its lower-right wall is the BACK and is the lower-left wall of
this picture; take its walls, tank and colours from it, but not its crane, whose jib is too long.
Paint the SAME building at the same size, turned on a turntable while the camera stays where it is.
It is not a mirror image and not a copy of any reference. The light stays where it is. It is
exactly as large as in the references: no taller, no lower, no storey more. Do not paint the
reference again.

Footprint, in pixels on the guide's 1024x1024 canvas (if your tool returns another size, scale
every number by its width / 1024 and keep the same places): the house's three outer corners at
ground level are w (353, 799), s (579, 911) and e (671, 865). The lower-left foot from w to s is
225 px long, the lower-right foot from s to e is 92 px, and the house is 317 px wide from w to e.
Nothing at ground level goes outside that diamond. The brick wall, foot to the top of its quoins
at the near corner s, is 136 to 149 px tall (the quoin top at about y 762 to 775 there); the steel
frame and the tank stand above it, the tank's top rim reaching about y 560 at s. Do not widen,
lengthen or lower the house.

Output: 1024x1024 RGBA PNG, transparent background, opaque surfaces.
Smooth painted contours, broad masses, three or four shades per material. Nothing at or above
#ECE4D0 and no yellow or orange as strong as #E8AA48. Never ground, plinth, grass, shadows outside
the base, rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow or
loose objects.
cornerReason: Read outer quoin base corners by eye: measureBase w falls inside the stepped quoin and s/e are fitted intersections.
